candidates.decision_relevance: The analyses repeatedly rely on 1-hour, 4-hour, 12-hour, 24-hour and 72-hour sequencing, but several windows are zero-span, shortened, or unavailable. A contiguous, timestamped BTC, ETH and ETH/BTC series with exact horizon anchors would materially distinguish transient endpoint moves from persistent continuation and reduce horizon-conflict uncertainty.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs from 2026-08-16 through 2026-08-18 repeatedly report unavailable 1h/4h anchors, zero-span 12h rows, and 60–68 hour nominal 72h windows.
candidates.metric_name: Contiguous exact-anchor BTC/ETH/ETH-BTC hourly price sequence
candidates.missing_history_problem: Current returns are based on inconsistent actual spans and cannot support reliable prospective horizon comparison.

candidates.decision_relevance: Breadth is central to the pullback and lifecycle interpretations, yet observations are mostly endpoints with changing membership hashes and no sustained path. Historical breadth using a stable, explicitly defined universe would test whether deterioration and recovery persisted rather than reflecting sampling or endpoint selection.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly review identifies the 29% breadth value as a single endpoint; daily outputs note differing membership hashes and absent comparable breadth history.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Advancer, decliner and flat-count changes are not reliably comparable across captures or distinguishable from transient endpoint noise.

candidates.decision_relevance: Funding, open interest, aggressive flow, depth, liquidations and option skew repeatedly disagree across assets and horizons. Retained synchronized histories with venue, unit and completeness metadata would materially improve attribution of price moves to leverage, flow or forced liquidation rather than relying on point-in-time snapshots and incomplete aggregates.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly cite mixed funding/OI/flow evidence, lower-bound liquidations with unverified completeness, and current-chain-only option observations.
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied evidence cannot separate persistent leverage buildup or liquidation pressure from measurement differences, capture timing, or already-realized positioning changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: ETF observations are used to assess BTC resilience and ecosystem transmission, but only isolated settled sessions are supplied. A retained daily history of settled BTC and ETH ETF flows would show whether the apparent support or divergence persisted across the relevant analysis windows.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly state that ETF data cover only one stale settled session, including 2026-08-14 or 2026-08-17, with no historical comparison.
candidates.metric_name: Settled BTC and ETH ETF net-flow history
candidates.missing_history_problem: Single-session totals cannot establish persistent inflow support, BTC/ETH divergence, or transmission beyond the observed endpoint.

candidates.decision_relevance: Rotation and transmission hypotheses repeatedly cannot be evaluated because BTC dominance, Total2, Total3 and stablecoin dominance histories are absent. Retaining these market-share and aggregate-capitalization series would provide the missing cross-market context for interpreting ETH/BTC weakness and breadth dispersion.
candidates.evidence_reference: Multiple daily outputs explicitly mark LKO-ROTATION-001, LKO-ROTATION-002 and LKO-TRANSMISSION-001 as unevaluable due to missing dominance, Total2/Total3 and stablecoin-dominance changes.
candidates.metric_name: Historical BTC dominance, Total2/Total3 and stablecoin-dominance series
candidates.missing_history_problem: ETH/BTC weakness cannot be distinguished between broad market contraction, BTC concentration, or genuine sector rotation without aggregate-market context.

candidates.decision_relevance: Macro evidence is disabled, stale, or lacks prior comparable values in the supplied analyses. A retained daily history of the referenced rates, dollar index and VIX would allow current crypto moves to be compared with contemporaneous macro shifts rather than leaving macro-related hypotheses unresolved.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly state that macro owners are disabled or stale and that no comparable prior macro observations are supplied.
candidates.missing_history_problem: The analyses cannot assess whether crypto weakness or resilience coincided with changing rates, dollar conditions or volatility.

candidates.decision_relevance: The weekly review states that three forecast candidates existed but their definitions and eventual outcomes are absent. Retained candidate specifications, formation timestamps, eligible information cutoffs and matured metric outcomes would materially assess descriptive hindsight versus prospective validity and range containment quality.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly adversarial review explicitly reports absent candidate definitions, bounds, reference prices, horizons, hit criteria and matured outcomes; daily outputs label candidates unratified.
candidates.metric_name: Historical forecast-candidate lifecycle and matured-outcome record
candidates.missing_history_problem: False positives, false negatives, containment quality, baseline comparison and hindsight leakage cannot be evaluated.
